cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the next right thing keeps showing up plain.
cells.ask: Take ten minutes and write down the one thing today that already has your attention. Then do that one first.
cells.core:
You can tell what actually matters here before you can explain why. Something in you keeps noticing which item on the list is the real one, and you have gotten used to trusting that pull without needing a committee to approve it. It doesn't arrive loud. It arrives like a small, steady lean, and you follow it.

Readiness looks like this: you don't spend the morning negotiating with yourself about which direction is legitimate, you turn toward the one that has weight and start. Help is already moving around you, and your part is to keep pointing at the true thing. Name the one that is already pulling, then act before the day dissolves it.
cells.sheetLine: You already pick the true thing. Keep picking it out loud.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future you are trying to write before it has happened.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest version of the plan and do one physical step of it today — open the file, make the call, buy the one item.
cells.core:
You are trying to settle the whole direction at once, ahead of time, so nothing can catch you off guard. Every open question gets pulled forward and examined — what if it goes this way, what if it goes that way — until planning becomes the thing you are doing all day. That work does feel like progress. It is not moving.

What you are reaching for is a version where the direction is fixed and safe, but directions don't work that way. They get chosen by walking one step of them. The excess is attention pointed forward instead of at what is actually in front of you now. You don't need more certainty about the whole route. You need one small physical move in the direction that was already pulling you before you started planning.
cells.sheetLine: You are planning the direction instead of taking one step in it.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, and you have not turned around.
cells.ask: Ask one person what they noticed you kept returning to last month, and write down the first thing they say without arguing with it.
cells.core:
There is a way of reading a room that used to work — you could feel which thing mattered and move toward it — and now the moving toward has stopped. Everything arrives with the same weight, and you wait for someone else to say which is real, and no one does, so nothing moves. The waiting is the part you're in.

The emptiness isn't in your judgment. It's in the part of you that used to turn a feeling into a step. Pushing yourself to just decide will not fill it. What fills it is tending something small and watching it grow, without forcing it — a plant, a page, a practice. Care that doesn't exhaust you puts current back through the line, and the sense of what matters starts to show itself again.
cells.sheetLine: The reading still works. The moving toward it stopped.

cells.tense: The pen is already down in a room you are still writing, and you call it someone else's handwriting.
cells.ask: Say 'this is mine' out loud about one thing you have been calling the work's or the group's, and notice if anything in your body disagrees.
cells.core:
You are already steering. People around you are following a direction you set — by what you say twice, what you let pass, what you agree to — and you file it under the work doing its own thing or the group going that way. You are the one picking the direction, and you are describing it as something that arrived on its own.

This isn't about taking credit in front of others. It's about the internal accounting, where your own direction keeps getting filed under circumstances. The help available here comes from outside, and it is the kind that holds weight while you look — a person who contains rather than corrects. Let someone be that. Naming one thing as yours doesn't overreach. It puts the pen back in your hand.
cells.sheetLine: You are already steering this. Nobody else is at the wheel.

attempts.check: The record supports a present capacity for direction and recognition, not a settled history, so any claim that the person has always known this, or knows exactly which star, is mine, not the map's. The reader could say 'I don't feel decisive at all,' and the cell must still give them something usable — the ask is noticing and naming what already draws attention, which survives being wrong because it only asks for one observation, not a verdict. The sentence serving the writer most is 'you already know,' because it can slide into flattery unless it stays tied to a concrete moment in the person's own day.
